clue.text: Mess she makes with buttery chocolate, as luck would have it

definitions.text: Mess she makes with buttery chocolate
definitions.meaning: a cookie, here a buttery chocolate biscuit, leaves a mess when it breaks into crumbs; cookie is also slang for a woman, the she
a resigned phrase meaning that is simply how fate turned out

explanation.surface: A woman makes a mess with a rich chocolate biscuit, and shrugs it off as bad luck.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading is literal: a buttery chocolate cookie making a mess as it breaks up. The second is the idiom of resignation.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom is said with a shrug when events turn out a certain way, so it stands for fate's chance outcome.

clue.text: Guardian's hot, Guardian's cold: gather round, following score — it doesn't stop at 12

parts.note: a score is twenty
F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references
the Guardian newspaper's crossword setters call the paper 'our'
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps
again the paper's own 'our'
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
to lock is to clasp or enclose, gathering something round in a hold

explanation.surface: A newspaper blows hot and cold while its readers gather round, apparently counting past twenty.
explanation.walkthrough: The score comes first in the answer although it ends the clue, because 'following' sits after it. The Guardian refers to itself as 'our' paper.
explanation.definitionFit: A timekeeping dial numbered 0 to 23 runs on past twelve rather than restarting, unlike an ordinary analogue face.

clue.text: Complaint of a Russian lake opening for trade

parts.note: Ilmen is a lake in north-west Russia, near Novgorod

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter, here taken from trade

explanation.surface: A Russian lake is opened up to commerce, prompting a grievance.
explanation.definitionFit: Complaint in its medical sense is an illness or disorder, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Shadow time by the 1down 21 saw start of Spanish succession problem

definitions.meaning: a time shown by the shadow on a sundial, read on the clock of 1 and 21 down, which shows five in the afternoon this way

definitions.text: saw start of Spanish succession problem
definitions.meaning: the year in which Charles II of Spain died childless, starting the War of the Spanish Succession

explanation.surface: A historical note on how time was told and on a royal inheritance crisis.
explanation.walkthrough: Charles II of Spain died in 1700, and the fight over his throne became the War of the Spanish Succession. On the clock of 1 and 21 down, 5pm is written as this.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are a number: an afternoon time of day as written in military style, and a year at the turn of a century.

clue.text: See 3
Fenland river all ____ good

definitions.meaning: the ... flows through the Fens of eastern England into the Wash
fill the gap to complete the stock phrase meaning fine, but with a reservation to follow

explanation.surface: A gap-fill exercise naming a river of the English Fens.
explanation.walkthrough: The Fens are the flat drained marshland of eastern England. The blank completes the phrase 'all ... good', said before a 'but'.
explanation.definitionFit: The river shares its name with the two words that complete the common phrase of grudging approval.

clue.text: End of 20 8 in German craft

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, taken here from the number written out

parts.note: the figure 20 is written out as twenty
acht is the German word for eight

explanation.surface: Reads as a cross-reference to other entries in the grid, ending in a German vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: '20 8' looks like references to 20 across and 8 down, but the figures are just numbers: twenty and eight.
explanation.definitionFit: A sailing or motor pleasure boat is a kind of craft, the general word for a vessel.

clue.text: Cabinet minister holding defence arrangements — a spear

indicators.note: one piece holds the other within it, so the minister's name goes round the defence letters

parts.note: Geoff Hoon was a British Cabinet minister in the Blair and Brown governments
ARP stands for Air Raid Precautions, Britain's wartime civil defence arrangements

explanation.surface: A Cabinet minister in charge of defence is armed with a spear.
explanation.walkthrough: Geoff Hoon was Defence Secretary, which makes the surface plausible; ARP is the Second World War Air Raid Precautions service.
explanation.definitionFit: A harpoon is a barbed spear thrown or fired at whales or large fish.

clue.text: See 1 across
Put sparkle into receding Fenland river around some villages

indicators.note: a river receding flows back, so the whole construction is read in the opposite direction
the river's name is placed around the other piece

parts.note: the Nene is a river of eastern England flowing through the Fens

indicators.note: only some of the word villages is used, its opening run of letters

explanation.surface: Bringing life to a Fenland river as it drains away from the local villages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Around' puts the river round the start of 'villages' (VIL, picked by 'some'), giving NEVILNE; 'receding' then turns the whole thing back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: To liven something up is to add sparkle or energy to it, a direct synonym.

clue.text: See what's on licence plate in place of pact

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning see or behold
a licence plate shows the car number, abbreviated as car no.

explanation.surface: Check the number plate to find where a treaty was signed.
explanation.walkthrough: The Locarno Treaties of 1925 were signed in the Swiss town of Locarno.
explanation.definitionFit: Locarno, in Switzerland, gave its name to the 1925 treaties settling post-war European borders.

clue.text: Wood in craft centre entries

indicators.note: the answer lies within the run of letters of these clue words

explanation.surface: Wooden items are on show in the entries of a craft centre.
explanation.definitionFit: Treen is a collective term for small wooden household objects, so wood made into things.

clue.text: Man of drift almost around a sacred river may have apple sauce

indicators.note: the shortened name is placed around the other letters
almost means the last letter is dropped from the name

parts.note: Rorke's Drift in Natal, scene of an 1879 battle, was named after the trader James Rorke
St, short for saint, a sacred person
the Po is the great river of northern Italy

explanation.surface: A drifter wanders around a holy river, a scene with no obvious link to Sunday lunch.
explanation.walkthrough: Rorke's Drift in South Africa is famous for its 1879 defence against the Zulus. 'Almost' drops the last letter of the man's name, leaving RORK.
explanation.definitionFit: Apple sauce is the classic British accompaniment to this roast meat, so the dish is defined by its condiment.

clue.text: Dad not quite dead — that's awfully silly

indicators.note: not quite the whole word, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: dad means father

indicators.note: awfully suggests the letters are put together badly, in a jumbled order

explanation.surface: Someone half-joking that their father is nearly dead, and being told off for it.
explanation.walkthrough: FATHE is FATHER 'not quite'; 'awfully' rearranges DEAD into ADED.
explanation.definitionFit: A fathead is a stupid person, so the adjective means foolish or silly.

clue.text: Show pain when caught in drink

indicators.note: the letter is placed inside the drink

parts.note: wine is a drink
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Someone grimaces when caught with a glass in hand.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket scorecards a batsman caught out is marked c.
explanation.definitionFit: To wince is to flinch or grimace, an outward show of pain.

clue.text: Ex-banker, a beast, gets intelligence in Australia

parts.note: a wolf is a wild beast

indicators.note: the intelligence goes inside the abbreviation for Australia

parts.note: Oz is the informal name for Australia
wit means intelligence or good sense

explanation.surface: A former banker is called a brute who learnt his smarts down under.
explanation.walkthrough: Paul Wolfowitz was President of the World Bank until 2007, when he resigned amid controversy.
explanation.definitionFit: Paul Wolfowitz headed the World Bank from 2005 to 2007, so he is a former banker.

clue.text: Ban Ki-moon or remove his powers?

definitions.meaning: Ban Ki-moon was Secretary-General of the United Nations
to take away a man's strength, courage or manhood

explanation.surface: Asks whether the UN chief should be stripped of his authority.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words, the answer describes the UN Secretary-General; read as one, it is a verb meaning to emasculate.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a person from the United Nations; the other is the verb meaning deprive of manly strength or nerve.

clue.text: In 2000, Nazism and Fascism kept the right from thinking of the left

indicators.note: the construction goes inside the Roman numeral

parts.note: MM is 2000 in Roman numerals

indicators.note: the alliance keeps the letter inside it

parts.note: the Axis was the alliance of Nazi Germany and Fascist Italy

explanation.surface: A political note that extreme right-wing ideologies were kept out of left-wing thought in 2000.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kept the right' looks like politics but is a container; 'In 2000' is not a date but a Roman numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: Marxism, the ideas of Karl Marx, is the foundational body of left-wing thought.

clue.text: Dot's follower, safe fellow about fifty, gives help in solving crossword

parts.note: in web addresses dot is followed by com

indicators.note: the safe goes round the numeral

parts.note: peter is criminal slang for a safe, and also a man's name
L is fifty in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Someone named Dot has a reliable friend in his fifties who finishes her crossword for her.
explanation.walkthrough: A peter is old underworld slang for a safe, hence safe-crackers being 'peter men'.
explanation.definitionFit: A completer is a book or list of answers that helps a solver finish the grid, a dictionary sense.

clue.text: Working lunch including direction for route of Eurostar

indicators.note: the rearranged letters include the direction within them
working suggests letters set in motion and rearranged

parts.note: NE is the compass direction north-east

explanation.surface: A working lunch on the train to Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Working' rearranges the letters of the lunch into CHUNL; 'including' puts the direction inside them, before the final L.
explanation.definitionFit: The Channel Tunnel, nicknamed with a blend of channel and tunnel, carries Eurostar trains between Britain and France.

clue.text: Heat absorber for containers needs service

parts.note: a table mat protects the surface from hot dishes
tins are containers

explanation.surface: Kitchen talk about mats and tins that turns to church.
explanation.definitionFit: Mattins, or matins, is the morning prayer service of the Anglican church.

clue.text: Patron of school finds article on God unfinished

indicators.note: in a down clue the second piece sits on, after, the first
the end of the word is left off

parts.note: the Trinity is God as Father, Son and Holy Spirit
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A school's patron saint is found in a piece about an incomplete deity.
explanation.walkthrough: St Trinian's is the fictional anarchic girls' school of Ronald Searle's cartoons and the films.
explanation.definitionFit: St Trinian, the notional saint of the cartoon girls' school, serves as its patron.

clue.text: Clay died in Nigerian port

indicators.note: the letter goes inside the port's name

parts.note: Port Harcourt is a major port city in Nigeria
D is the abbreviation for died, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: Someone named Clay died in a West African port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clay' looks like a person's name, but it is a tennis surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A clay tennis court is one type of hard (as opposed to grass) court surface.

clue.text: See 1
Poppy's first piece has some musical backing

parts.note: Op. I, opus one, is a composer's first piece

indicators.note: backing turns the letters round so they read in reverse
only some of the word musical is used, its first two letters

explanation.surface: A child named Poppy plays her first composition with a musical accompaniment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poppy's' looks like a girl's name but is the flower: opium comes from the poppy. MU, 'some musical', is turned round by 'backing'.
explanation.definitionFit: Opium is the drug extracted from the opium poppy, so it is the poppy's product.

clue.text: Fighter for crown in Punic or Napoleonic wars

indicators.note: the answer lies within the run of letters of these clue words

explanation.surface: A warrior fighting for a throne in ancient or nineteenth-century wars.
explanation.walkthrough: In the nursery rhyme the lion and the unicorn were fighting for the crown; they are the supporters of the UK royal arms.
explanation.definitionFit: The nursery rhyme has the lion and this beast battling for the crown, as on the royal coat of arms.

clue.text: Opening letter

definitions.meaning: first or beginning, as an adjective
the first letter of a name

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both an adjective meaning first or beginning and a noun for a name's first letter.

clue.text: Seeks, with zoom lens's potential, places commoner since July

indicators.note: the potential of the letters is what else they could be arranged to form

parts.note: taken as written, the possessive letters included

explanation.surface: A photographer seeks what a zoom lens could capture.
explanation.walkthrough: England banned smoking in enclosed public places from 1 July 2007, when this puzzle appeared, so smoke-free places multiplied.
explanation.definitionFit: Areas where smoking or smoke emission is banned became far more widespread after the July smoking ban.
